result:
If I had to pick just one, I think I'd make it so that people could reliably tell when they're wrong.

Not omniscience—just an honest internal signal. Something that lit up when your confidence had outrun your evidence, or when you'd stopped listening because you'd already decided.

It sounds modest next to "end hunger" or "cure disease," but I keep coming back to it because so many of the big problems aren't really knowledge problems. We often know what would help. What blocks us is that people—individually and in groups—get locked into positions and can't update. Wars drag on because leaders can't admit a mistake. Institutions decay because no one inside can see what outsiders see plainly. Even in ordinary life, a huge amount of suffering comes from two people who each feel certain, talking past each other.

If that got fixed, a lot of other things might start fixing themselves.

I'll admit it's also a bit self-interested as a choice. I make errors, and I don't always know when I'm doing it. A world where being wrong was easier to notice and less shameful to acknowledge would be one I'd find a lot more comfortable to exist in.

What about you—what would you change?
